article_title: Hybrid teaching after COVID-19: advantages, challenges and optimization strategies.
citation: Wang Xiaoran, Liu Jiangheng, Jia Shuwei, Hou Chunmei, Jiao Runsheng, Yan Yan, Ma Tengchuang, Zhang Ying, Liu Yanyan, Wen Haixia, Wang Yu-Feng, Zhu Hui, Liu Xiao-Yu. (2024). title: HBOPPPS hybrid teaching model with online resource library for Physiology at Harbin Medical University
description: HBOPPPS is a hybrid teaching method introduced in 2019 that incorporates online instructional techniques into the offline BOPPPS framework (Bridge-in, Objective, Pre-assessment, Participatory learning, Post-assessment, Summary). The team built an online resource set including "course-associated micro-lecture videos (85 in total, 5 ∼ 10 min/video)", science stories, lectures by renowned doctors, virtual simulation experiments and chapter tests. Pre-class course guidance was delivered through the "Xuexi Tong" mobile application, with in-class interactive elements such as sign-in procedures, multi-choice questions and task allocation.
requirements: An established offline BOPPPS teaching model
An online learning resource library and a mobile application for course guidance and interaction
constraints: Implemented for Physiology teaching at Harbin Medical University among undergraduate medical students
target_learners: Undergraduate medical students in Pharmacy, Clinical Pharmacy, Basic Medicine and Clinical Medicine programs
target_learning_goals: Understanding healthy human body functions in Physiology, linking preclinical and clinical courses
examples: Students received pre-class course guidance via the Xuexi Tong app covering course objectives and key knowledge, and used in-class online sign-in, quiz and response functions
